title: Geometric Aspects of Entanglement
authors: Lucio De Simone, Lorenzo Capra, Arthur Vesperini, Leonardo Rossi, Loris Di Cairano, Roberto Franzosi
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource in quantum information theory, yet its general characterization and quantification remain challenging, especially in multipartite systems. In this work we investigate entanglement from a geometric perspective, focusing on the Riemannian structure induced by the Fubini--Study metric on the projective Hilbert space of multi-qubit quantum states. By exploiting the local-unitary invariance of this metric, we derive the entanglement distance (ED), a geometric measure that quantifies entanglement as an obstruction to locally minimizing the sum of squared Fubini--Study distances generated by local operations.   We analyze the properties of ED for pure multi-qubit states and discuss its behavior under local operations and classical communication. In particular, we show that ED reproduces established entanglement measures in well-defined and restricted settings. For pure states of two qubits, ED reduces to an exact monotone function of the concurrence and, independently, to an explicit monotone function of the entropy of entanglement. These results provide a clear geometric interpretation of standard bipartite entanglement measures within the present framework, while highlighting the limitations of such correspondences beyond the two-qubit case.
summary: This work introduces the Entanglement Distance (ED), a novel geometric measure derived from the Fubini-Study metric on the projective Hilbert space to quantify quantum entanglement. By exploiting the geometry of local operations, the ED provides a rigorous, intrinsic measure that successfully reproduces known entanglement monotones for two-qubit systems. It offers a deep geometric interpretation of quantum correlations for multipartite systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide a geometric characterization and quantification of quantum entanglement, particularly in complex multipartite systems.
main_result: The derived Entanglement Distance (ED) is shown to be a geometric measure that quantifies entanglement as an obstruction to local minimization, reproducing established measures like concurrence for two qubits.
method: The methodology involves analyzing the Riemannian structure induced by the Fubini-Study metric on the projective Hilbert space of multi-qubit states.
model_or_system: The system under study consists of multi-qubit quantum states, treated mathematically on the projective Hilbert space PH. The analysis focuses on the geometry induced by local unitary transformations.
key_observables: Entanglement Distance (ED), Concurrence, Entropy of Entanglement, Fubini-Study metric tensor.
important_parameters: The number of qubits (M), the specific local unitary transformations applied.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on exploiting the local-unitary invariance of the Fubini-Study metric, though the correspondence with standard measures is noted to be limited beyond the two-qubit case.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the geometric framework using the Fubini-Study metric on PH. It then derives the entanglement measure (ED) based on local-unitary invariance. Finally, it analyzes the properties of ED, showing its equivalence to known measures in the bipartite two-qubit case.
why_interesting: The geometric approach offers a powerful, intrinsic mathematical tool to quantify entanglement, potentially providing a unified framework applicable to complex, high-dimensional quantum systems beyond simple bipartite settings.
